title: Defaults for the Common Case
content:
What problem does this solve?
Some function arguments have a common value most of the time. **Default parameter values** let callers omit that argument while keeping the option to override it.

Basic syntax
  def mark_route(destination, status="Review"):
      return f"{destination}: {status}"
  print(mark_route("Gloamfen"))
  print(mark_route("Ash Ford", "Ready"))

What actually happens
- Required parameters come first
- Omitting an optional argument uses its declared default
- Passing a value overrides the default
- Keyword arguments bind by name

When this is useful
Make calling code simple for common cases while keeping flexibility.
concepts: Required parameters come before defaulted parameters
Omitting an optional argument uses the default

examples.title: Declared default
examples.explanation: Without a second argument, status takes the declared default.

common_mistakes: Putting a required parameter after a defaulted one
Using a list or dictionary default (can be dangerous — mention only)

exercises.title: Use the declared default
hints: status has a default of Review.
Calling with one argument uses the default for status.

exercises.title: Which signature is valid?
exercises.prompt: Which function signature is valid in Python?
exercises.success_message: Correct — required parameters come before defaults.
exercises.failure_message: Defaults come after required parameters, and quotes are not used in parameter names.
hints: Parameter names are identifiers, not quoted strings.

exercises.title: One item by default
exercises.prompt: Add a default so quantity is 1 when omitted.
hints: Declare the default in the function signature.

exercises.title: Required before optional
exercises.prompt: Fix the parameter order so the function is valid.
hints: destination is required; status is optional.

exercises.title: Dispatch log entry
exercises.prompt:
Write log_entry(message, level="NOTICE", source="field") returning:

    [<level>][<source>] <message>

Require the exact parameter order and declared defaults.
hints: Build the string with the brackets around level and source.
Defaults should match exactly: NOTICE and field.
Keyword arguments can override either default.
exercises.success_message: I can make a function convenient for the common case without hiding its inputs.
